doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Advice, education and the evolution of jazz
title: Younger musicians with a business mind: Ron Carter and Carl Allen
summary: Golson names Ron Carter and Carl Allen as great musicians with foresight, imagination and common sense.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Have there been any others in his generation that have inspired you, that you feel [are] worthy of mentioning?
I consider him the generation before Wynton’s.

Carl Allen, businessman, who now heads up the jazz program at Juilliard. These are people – great musicians – but they’ve got a business mind too. They’re not – they don’t have any prescient power, that is, to see into the future, but they use common sense. So they have a certain perspicacity, because of what’s going on now, what the possibilities are tomorrow. They draw from that and use their imagination, like you say, which is inherent to creativity. Creativity without imagination is nothing. It begins – you have to have that imagination to bring about life to the things that you imagine, which is your creativity. Those kinds of people, they have that ability to look ahead. They don’t have a glass ball. If you can put two and two together – syllogistically reasoning. This goes with that. Then that can possibly grow out of that. You get your syllogistic thinking together, and then you can forecast and bring things into existence that had no prior existence. That’s what they’re able to do.
